source_title: The Weir Group Annual Report and Financial Statements 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 73 and 142 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 26 February 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Reported revenue rose 9% to £2,662m but fell 6% like for like, while adjusted operating margin contracted 100bps to 13.2% and adjusted profit before tax fell 2% to £303m. A £546m Oil & Gas North America impairment drove a £379m reported loss after tax. Free cash flow reversed from a £109m inflow to a £79m outflow, net debt rose to £1,157m and covenant leverage increased to 2.46x, although mining businesses delivered strong growth.
already_announced_exclusion: The completed Oil & Gas cost-reduction programme, £35m annualised savings, Flow Control disposal, ESCO integration actions and disclosed Minerals and Oil & Gas restructuring and rationalisation actions are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The large impairment, statutory loss, like-for-like decline, margin contraction, cash outflow and elevated leverage create high pressure. Strong Minerals and ESCO performance and positive operating cash generation provide meaningful but limited offsets.

source_title: The Weir Group Annual Report and Financial Statements 2021
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 82 and 163 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 2 March 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Orders rose 22%, revenue increased 2% and adjusted operating profit 5% on a constant-currency basis, with adjusted margin improving to 15.3% and statutory operating profit rising 13%. A cybersecurity incident and working-capital build reduced operating cash flow 27% to £266m and free cash flow to £62m, but net debt fell £279m to £772m and covenant leverage improved to 1.9x after the Oil & Gas disposal.
already_announced_exclusion: The completed Oil & Gas division disposal, initial efficiency-programme actions and other restructuring or portfolio actions disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Cyber disruption and weaker cash conversion create moderate cash pressure. Record orders, constant-currency growth, margin improvement, falling debt and ample covenant headroom provide very strong contrary evidence.

source_title: The Weir Group Annual Report and Financial Statements 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 71 and 148 state that the strategic report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 29 February 2024; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 7% to £2,636m, adjusted operating profit increased 16% to £459m, adjusted margin expanded 140bps to 17.4% and statutory profit before tax rose 23%. Operating cash flow increased 17% to £526m, free cash flow reached £238m, net debt fell £107m to £690m and covenant leverage improved to 1.1x. The report separately disclosed £28.8m of Performance Excellence programme costs.
already_announced_exclusion: The announced Performance Excellence programme, capacity optimisation, service-centre restructuring, facility relocations, global business services programme, Russia wind-down and other disclosed rationalisation actions are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Strong revenue and profit growth, substantial margin expansion, robust cash generation, falling debt and low leverage provide exceptionally strong contrary evidence. Announced efficiency actions are excluded rather than treated as future targets.
